cohort: Bangladeshi women who delivered between 2004 and 2017, whose data was collected via the Bangladesh Demographic and Health Surveys.
finding: The prevalence of cesarean section (CS) in Bangladesh increased from 4.50% in 2004 to 32.73% in 2017, and significant socioeconomic and geographical inequalities in CS delivery were observed.
mod_finding: Significant socioeconomic inequalities in CS were found to be pro-rich and concentrated among higher educated women, alongside geographical disparities with higher concentrations in urban areas and a coastal region.
